scenarioComparison.interpretation: The sampled PSS/Java peaks are close, while B8 native-allocated peak and final process footprint are higher. Durations, extra dual open/close phases, actual camera drift, peak timing and cache state differ, so this is not an isolated causal memory delta. Each run shows a static 60-second contour/render tail. B8's first 20 seconds after close still had frame-count changes and high CPU; its following 60-second tail was quiet.

findings: MvtBatchedLineTile.releaseRenderResources removes only its VBO/EBO RenderResourceCache keys; it does not cancel entries in the current Frame UploadQueue.

RenderContext.offerGLBufferUpload wraps the existing vertex/element arrays in NumericArray and queues them; UploadQueue entries retain both array and BufferObject until processUploads recycles them or Frame.recycle clears the queue.

BasicFrameController.drawFrame processes queued uploads before drawable submission; Frame.recycle calls clearUploads. This establishes a possible short render-to-GL-frame retention window after a tile's cache keys are removed.

No A8/B8 counter measured queued upload bytes or release-time queue depth, and the static tails were stable. The source path is a bounded transient possibility, not evidence that uploads caused the sampled peaks or the reported phone crash.

limits: A8 Java heap sample peak was 496.13/512 MiB and B8 495.39/512 MiB; these are sampled transient used values, not post-GC retained heap.
No sampled tuple exceeded reported Java max; approximate Runtime counters do not prove absence of OOM risk.
No target-PID OOM/FATAL/ANR/signal/death entries in captured windows is not proof of phone stability or a unique cause.
Persistent preview capture was present in the environment; no per-run encoder snapshot was recorded for A8/B8.
Android Window FrameMetrics measure HWUI, not WorldWind GL/GPU time; map frame count/frame age are output cadence, not FPS.
No source budget, contour detail, style, interval or cache capacity changed for C8.
